notes: Tilanusstraat 23K (BAG, 2013; Amsterdam-Oost, Eerste Boerhaavestraat side): a block of red-brick gridded wings, a curved glass tower with stacked louvre bands on the Tilanusstraat corner and, along the east side, a retained 1900s brick school range with a stone oriel. 117 3DBAG wall surfaces; three street fronts are drawn (w01-160 south, w02-250 west tower, w03-340 north), the rest stays blank.

walls[0] = panel 32 (S, 77 m, eaves 18.5): red clinker brick with deep-set paired windows in gridded bays, drawn as 5 storeys x 18 bays of narrow windows; the stepped upper floors (31.9 m surfaces) and the curved corner are straight/blank. walls[1] = panel 33 (W, 46 m, eaves 31.9): the louvred tower front, a glazed ground storey (shop/lobby) under eight bands of grey louvres and glass; drawn as ribbon-windows, 8 storeys x 6 bays of wide windows in a grey stone-material skin. The real front is a curved glass skin with continuous aluminium louvre blades: the curve and the louvres are not modelled (a curtain-wall grid was tried and read as a square grid). walls[2] = panel 6 (N, 37 m, eaves 15.5): dark brown brick with tall paired windows, 4 storeys x 9 bays.

Not drawn: the retained brick school range with its stone oriel and blue-brick plinth band (w04-70, east side; it matches no unambiguous 3DBAG panel: panels 2 and 13 share one party-wall footprint with the new wing) and the lobby entrance on the tower front; the east, courtyard and scaffolded fronts (w07-70 is under scaffolding).
